Here's a summary of what the search turned up. Most results are third-party guides rather than Anthropic's official docs, so treat the specifics as community advice.

**Core structure**
- Skill files live in a folder with a SKILL.md at the top. One guide describes the folder as a folder at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ containing a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter and markdown instructions.
- Required frontmatter is the name and description. The same guide says the description is the trigger, and most of your writing time belongs there, not on the body.
- Supporting scripts, templates, and reference docs are optional and can sit in the same directory, referenced from SKILL.md.

**Writing the description**
- One guide advises using gerund-style names such as "writing-release-notes" and making the description specific. It also suggests a test: ask Claude to do the task without the slash command, then check whether the skill loaded. If not, the description is too vague.

**Keeping skills lean**
- Skills load progressively. One source notes that at startup only the name and description of each skill are loaded, and the full SKILL.md only gets read when relevant.
- Another guide recommends first asking whether Claude actually needs the skill, by testing its baseline performance without one.

**Process and testing**
- A TDD-style approach is suggested: write test scenarios, watch the agent fail without the skill, write the skill, then refine it to close loopholes.
- Skills are best for reusable techniques, patterns, or reference material. Project-specific conventions belong in CLAUDE.md instead.

**Gaps**
- None of the results quoted Anthropic's official best-practices page directly, so verify exact field rules and length guidance against the official Claude Code docs.

The search didn't return Anthropic's official authoring best-practices page. The useful material comes from Anthropic's engineering post and third-party write-ups.

- **Progressive disclosure, per Anthropic's engineering post:** The name and description load at startup, which gives enough to decide when a skill applies. If Claude thinks the skill is relevant to the current task, it will load the skill by reading its full SKILL.md into context. Bundled files are read only when needed. Agents with a filesystem and code execution tools don't need to read the entirety of a skill into their context window.
- **Description guidance (third-party):** One write-up says descriptions should be written in the third person, state what the skill does and when to use it, and avoid summarizing the workflow. It attributes the last point to Anthropic's testing, which found the model then follows the description instead of reading the body. Anthropic's own testing showed the model then follows the description instead of reading the body. I couldn't confirm this against Anthropic's own documentation.
- **Structure:** name+description always in system prompt (~100 tok/skill) → body on trigger (<5k tok) → resources/scripts on demand. This is also a third-party summary.
- **Caveat:** The Tessl pages are auto-generated quality reviews of a community "apply-anthropic-skill-best-practices" skill, not Anthropic material. One of them notes that the guide is verbose, so treat it as secondary.

For the official wording, check Anthropic's Agent Skills documentation directly. I'd suggest a follow-up search for "Claude Code skills docs" or the skill-authoring page on docs.anthropic.com.

content.text:
Here is what the searches turned up. Most of it is community advice. Anthropic's official best-practices page didn't appear in either search, so check the exact rules, such as field limits and length guidance, against the official docs.

**Structure**
- A skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md`. That file has YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) followed by markdown instructions.
- Scripts, templates, and reference docs can sit alongside it and be linked from `SKILL.md`.
- Skills load in stages, which Anthropic calls progressive disclosure:
  - Only the name and description load at startup, at roughly 100 tokens per skill.
  - The `SKILL.md` body loads when Claude judges the skill relevant. One third-party source suggests keeping it under about 5k tokens.
  - Bundled files and scripts load only when needed.

**Description**
- The description is what triggers the skill, so most of your writing effort belongs there.
- State what the skill does and when to use it.
- Write it in the third person.
- Don't summarize the workflow in the description. One write-up says the model then follows the description instead of reading the body. I couldn't confirm that against Anthropic's own documentation.
- To test it, ask Claude to do the task without invoking the skill by name. If the skill doesn't load, the description is too vague.

**Naming and scope**
- Use specific, gerund-style names, such as `writing-release-notes`.
- Skills suit reusable techniques, patterns, and reference material. Project-specific conventions belong in `CLAUDE.md`.

**Content**
- Keep the body lean and move detail into separate reference files.
- Check first whether Claude needs the skill at all by testing its baseline performance without one.

**Process**
- Develop skills like tests:
  - Write test scenarios.
  - Watch the agent fail without the skill.
  - Write the skill.
  - Refine it to close loopholes.

Sources:
- [How to create a Claude Code skill (and the best practices nobody put in the docs)](https://codemeetai.substack.com/p/how-to-create-a-claude-code-skill)
- [Lessons from building Claude Code: How we use skills](https://claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills)
- [How to Write Skills for Claude Code and Cowork](https://sherlock.xyz/post/how-to-write-skills-for-claude-code-and-cowork)
- [skill writing (skills.sh)](https://www.skills.sh/meriley/claude-code-skills/skill-writing)
- [Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills (Anthropic Engineering)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)
- [Production-grade agent skills authoring guide 2026](https://noqta.tn/en/blog/production-grade-agent-skills-authoring-guide-2026)
- [Agent Skills: Progressive Disclosure as a System Design Pattern](https://www.newsletter.swirlai.com/p/agent-skills-progressive-disclosure)
